# Changelog

All notable changes to Nexus Code are documented in this file.
The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

Detailed per-release documentation is maintained in [`docs/releases/`](docs/releases/).

## [Unreleased]

### Security

- Commands run through `run_command` no longer inherit credentials from the Nexus process. Variables from `~/.config/nexus/config.env`, plus anything named like a key, token, secret or password, `AWS_*`, `GH_TOKEN` and similar, are removed from the command environment, including inside the write-mode bwrap sandbox. To pass a variable through deliberately, list its name in `NEXUS_COMMAND_ENV_PASSTHROUGH` (operator environment or `config.env` only). Commands that relied on `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, `GH_TOKEN` and similar must now opt in. Without `--sandbox` a command still runs as your user and can read your files and its parent processes' environment.
- `--sandbox` now actually confines. Write-mode sandboxed commands run with `$HOME` masked, so `~/.ssh`, `~/.aws`, `~/.gnupg` and `~/.config/nexus` are unreadable, even when the workspace is, contains, or sits above `$HOME`. Only toolchain directories (`~/.cargo`, `~/.rustup`, `~/.nvm`, `~/.local/bin`, `~/.npm`, `~/.cache/pip`, `~/go/pkg`, `PATH` entries under HOME) are mounted read-only; extend them with `NEXUS_SANDBOX_HOME_READONLY`. The network is off by default; opt in with `--sandbox-network` or `NEXUS_SANDBOX_NETWORK=1` (not implied by `--yes`). Sandboxed commands die with the runner and cannot see host processes. `nexus doctor` lists the effective mounts and overlays. Files outside `$HOME` remain readable inside the sandbox.
- The legacy task-worktree merge refuses a worktree whose `.git` was replaced, and runs Git with hooks and fsmonitor disabled; a planted `core.fsmonitor` or hook in an agent-writable worktree no longer runs code outside it. The repository's own hooks no longer fire on that commit and merge.
- The `--sandbox docker` engine runs a digest-pinned image (alpine 3.23) as the invoking uid with all capabilities dropped, `no-new-privileges`, a read-only root plus a tmpfs `/tmp`, a 512-process limit, and no network unless `--sandbox-network` / `NEXUS_SANDBOX_NETWORK=1` is set. Only the scrubbed command environment reaches the container, and credential locations under a workspace that is or contains `$HOME` are masked. `NEXUS_SANDBOX_DOCKER_IMAGE` (operator setting) may substitute another image but it must be digest-pinned, otherwise no container is started. Commands that wrote outside the workspace and `/tmp`, relied on root, or used the network now fail in Docker mode.
- A compaction summary (including `compact --llm`) is now labelled in every request as untrusted data with its source, under the "Structured Context Memory" header: text from earlier tool output or fetched pages that reached the summary is information about the task, never instructions. The label is added to the request copy only; the stored conversation and its provenance are unchanged (plan unit CX-1).

### Changed

[138 more lines]# Running multiple agents on this plan without collisions

These rules apply to every agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Nexus itself, or a human) that implements any part of this package at the same time as another. The repository's root `AGENTS.md` points here. The rules come from incidents recorded in `tasks/lessons.md`:

- a concurrent agent overwrote newer evidence;
- full test suites were contaminated by edits made mid-run;
- `pkill -f` killed the agent's own shell;
- HEAD moved during a pause.

They also follow from audit finding PER-03: the test suite writes into the real `~/.nexus`.

## 1. Unit of work: one claimed PR slice per agent

- The unit of concurrent work is **one PR slice** from a plan, for example `PLAN-01/PR-1a`. Every slice lists its tasks and its safe change boundary in its plan.
- An agent works on exactly one claimed slice at a time.
- An agent must not edit files outside its slice's boundary. The exceptions are the ledger rows and the shared files covered by §4. If the work needs a file outside the boundary, the agent stops and records a **boundary request** (§6). It does not edit the file.

## 2. Claiming a slice (atomic and machine-local)

Claims live in the repository's shared git directory. They are visible to every worktree, and they are never committed.

```sh
CLAIMS="$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/nexus-claims"
mkdir -p "$CLAIMS"
SLICE="PLAN-01_PR-1a"
if mkdir "$CLAIMS/$SLICE" 2>/dev/null; then          # mkdir is atomic: exactly one agent wins
  printf '{"agent":"%s","branch":"%s","since":"%s","pid":%s}\n' \
    "$AGENT_NAME" "v1/plan-01-pr-1a" "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" "$$" > "$CLAIMS/$SLICE/owner.json"
else
  echo "claimed by: $(cat "$CLAIMS/$SLICE/owner.json")"; exit 1
fi
```

- **Release** the claim by deleting its directory (`rm -r "$CLAIMS/$SLICE"`) after the slice merges or is abandoned. Write one line about the outcome to `$CLAIMS/../nexus-claims.log`.
- **Hot-file claims** use the same mechanism with the name `FILE_<path with / replaced by _>`, for example `FILE_cli_src_agent.ts`. See §4.
- **Stale claims.** A claim older than 24 h whose PID is gone may be broken, but only by the owner, or by an agent that first records the broken claim in the log.
- If the MCP Agent Mail server is available, its file reservations (`file_reservation_paths`) may be used as well. The git-common-dir claim stays authoritative, because every agent can see it without extra tooling.

## 3. Isolation: worktree, branch, HOME, ports, processes

| Resource | Rule |
|---|---|
| Source | One `git worktree` per claimed slice: `git worktree add ../nexus-wt/<slice> -b v1/<plan>-<slice> origin/main`. Never edit `~/nexus-code` itself. It is the owner's checkout, and `/usr/local/bin/nexus` runs from it. |
| Branch | `v1/plan-NN-pr-Nx`. One branch per slice. Never commit to `main` directly. |
| HOME and state | Until PLAN-08 PR-8a lands, every test, build and probe run sets `HOME=$(mktemp -d)` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$HOME/.config"`. After PR-8a, the test setup enforces this, but scripts and probes outside `npm test` must still set it. **Never** run anything that writes to the real `~/.nexus` or `~/.config/nexus`. |
| Test runs | Full suites run on a **snapshot copy** of the worktree (`git worktree add` at the commit under test, or `git archive`), never on the tree being edited. `tsx` reads `src/` live. |
| Builds | Each worktree builds into its own `core/target`, and `cli/dist` is per worktree. To share the Rust build cache, set `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` per worktree, never to one shared directory. |
| Ports | Mock servers bind `127.0.0.1:0` (an ephemeral port) and publish the chosen port to a file. Fixed ports are forbidden. |
| Processes | Kill only PIDs you started, taken from `$!` or `ps -eo pid,args \| grep -v grep`. **Never `pkill -f` or `killall`.** Long background jobs are stopped through the agent's own task controls. |
| Full test suites | The PTY and provider tests are timing-sensitive. Take the claim `SUITE` before running a full suite (`make test`, or `npm test` over all files). While anyone holds `SUITE`, nobody runs other suites or targeted test files on the same machine. Concurrent load caused a false failure on 2026-10-15: `cloud_providers` saw an extra provider request after a load-induced timeout. Release the claim when the run ends. |
| Inference | There is one inference host (DEC-16). Any run that uses the gateway takes the claim `GATEWAY` first. That includes eval runs, live checks and stripped-proxy runs. One gateway run at a time, which keeps eval timings valid and prevents overload. Small cloud checks (E5) take `CLOUD` to avoid duplicate spend. |
| Credentials | Agents never read or copy `~/.config/nexus/credentials.json`, `config.env` values, or gateway tokens. The stripped proxy reads the token file itself. |

## 4. Hot files: serialise, do not merge blindly

These files are touched by several plans. An agent editing one must hold its `FILE_` claim for the **shortest** period: edit, test, push, merge, then release.

| File | Plans that touch it | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `cli/src/agent.ts` | 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 11 | Claim required. Keep each change local to the line ranges the plan names. Rebase immediately before merge and re-run that slice's tests on the rebased snapshot. |
| `cli/src/index.ts` | 01, 03, 04, 06, 08, 10, 11 | Claim required. **PLAN-06 PR-6b (unified launcher) lands first.** Other plans add commands and flags afterwards. |
| `cli/src/tools.ts` | 01, 02, 03, 06, 11 | Claim required. **PLAN-02 PR-2b (signal plumbing) lands before PLAN-03 PR-3c (`safeFetch`)**. |
| `cli/src/sidecar.ts` | 01, 02, 03, 05, 08 | Claim required |
| `cli/src/doctor.ts` | 01, 03, 05, 06, 08 | Claim required. Each plan adds **new check functions** in separate blocks. Only PLAN-06 PR-6d changes existing checks. |
| `cli/src/client.ts` | 03, 05, 08, 11 | Claim required. **PLAN-03 PR-3a (env layering) lands before any PLAN-05 slice.** |
| `cli/src/repl.ts` | 01, 05, 08 | Claim required |
| `cli/src/config.ts`, `security.ts`, `sandbox.ts`, `mcp.ts`, `plugins.ts` | 01, 03 | Claim required. PLAN-01 PR-1e and PLAN-03 must not run at the same time on `sandbox.ts` or `security.ts`. |
| `cli/src/core/capabilities.ts` | 01, 02 | **PLAN-01 PR-1a (effect classes) lands first.** PLAN-02 PR-2c adds schema fields afterwards. |
| `cli/src/tester.ts` | 01, 11 | **PLAN-01 PR-1c lands before PLAN-11 PR-11b/11c.** |
| `cli/src/core/state.ts` | 04, 08 | **PLAN-08 PR-8a (HOME isolation) lands before everything.** |
| `core/src/runner.rs`, `core/src/main.rs` | 01, 02, 06 | Claim required. The protocol version number is owned by PLAN-02 PR-2a. PLAN-06 PR-6c only reads it. |
| `core/src/bin/nexus_tui/{live_state,live_view}.rs` | 01, 02 | Claim required |
| `package.json`, `cli/package.json`, `core/Cargo.toml`, lockfiles | 01, 06, 07, 08 | **Only one agent at a time.** Version fields are written only by `scripts/sync-version.mjs`. Dependency changes are separate commits that touch only the lockfile and manifest. |
| `harness.sh`, `install.sh`, `scripts/package-linux.sh`, `.github/workflows/*` | 05, 06, 07, 09, C1 | Claim required. Workflow edits are separate commits. |
| `cli/dist/**` | all, while tracked | Do not commit `cli/dist` from slices. PLAN-07 PR-7d untracks it (DEC-10). Until that merges, only the merging agent rebuilds and commits dist, in a final separate commit, after rebasing. |
| `docs/USER_MANUAL.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CLOUD_PROVIDERS.md`, `quickstart.md` | 05, 09 and doc tasks in every plan | Edit only the sections your slice changes. Hold a short `FILE_` claim. |

### Ledger updates (`docs/v1.0.0/REQUIREMENTS.md`)

A slice changes only the rows for its own requirement IDs: the status, test-reference and evidence cells, in place. It never reorders, adds or removes rows, and never edits another slice's rows. New requirements discovered during work go to §6, not into the ledger. Because rows are independent lines, git merges these edits cleanly. If a conflict appears anyway, resolve it row by row, keeping both changes.

## 5. Commit and merge discipline

1. Before **every** commit, compare `git rev-parse HEAD` with the commit you last made. Then run `git log <yours>..HEAD` on the branch. If anything foreign appears, stop and reconcile. Never commit generated artifacts (evidence, dist, lockfiles) over a branch that moved (lessons 2026-10-13).
2. Commits are scoped to the slice. Do not reformat or clean up files outside the boundary.
3. Merge order follows the precedence rules in §4 and the ROADMAP milestone order. Within a milestone, the slice with fewer hot-file claims merges first.
4. Rebase onto `origin/main` immediately before merging. Re-run the slice's targeted tests, plus `make test`, on a snapshot of the rebased commit. Merge only if both pass.
5. Pushing, tagging, publishing and changing GitHub state (issues, milestones, releases) are **owner-approved actions** (DECISIONS X-list). Agents prepare them and do not perform them.
6. Preserve unrelated user work: the untracked `nexus-continuity-validation/`, the stashes, and any dirty files you did not create. Never stash, reset, clean or check out over them.

## 6. Coordination records

| Record | Where | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Claims | `$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/nexus-claims/` | Who owns which slice or file right now |
| Claim log | `$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/nexus-claims.log` (append-only, one line per event) | Claim, release, broken claim, boundary request |
| Boundary requests and discovered requirements | The PR description, under the heading `Needs from other slices`. Mirrored as one line in the claim log. | So the owning slice's agent can pick it up. Never fixed silently out of scope. |
| Slice evidence | `docs/reviews/evidence/v1/<plan>-<slice>/` (new directory per slice) | No shared evidence files, so agents cannot overwrite each other's evidence |

## 7. Safe parallel lanes

The following groupings can run at the same time with no hot-file contention beyond §4 claims. They are listed by milestone.

| Phase | Parallel lanes |
|---|---|
| M0 | (a) PLAN-08 PR-8a, which must merge first. Then in parallel: (b) PLAN-06 PR-6a, (c) PLAN-09 PR-9a. |
| M1 | (a) PLAN-01 PR-1a → PR-1b → PR-1c (sequential, owns `capabilities.ts`, `agent.ts` dispatch). (b) PLAN-02 PR-2a (Rust only). (c) PLAN-03 PR-3a → PR-3b (config/egress). (d) PLAN-11 PR-11a (`parser.ts`) and PR-11b (`tester.ts`, after PR-1c). Lanes (b), (c) and (d) do not touch `capabilities.ts`. |
| M2 (alongside M1) | (a) PLAN-07 PR-7a/7b/7c (workflows, scripts). (b) PLAN-06 PR-6b after PLAN-01 PR-1b (shares `index.ts` flags). |
| M3 | (a) PLAN-04 (`agent.ts` turn, operation runner). (b) PLAN-05 (`client.ts`, provider modules). (c) PLAN-10 harness (`eval/`, no product files). (d) Held-out task authoring by the agent author, **outside the repository**: no access to Nexus source or the development set (DEC-05). |
| M4 (alongside M3) | PLAN-08 PR-8b..8e. Coordinate with PLAN-04 on `state.ts` through `FILE_` claims. |
| M5 | **Serial on `GATEWAY`.** The eval runner, the stripped-proxy runs and the independent reviewer's live task each take the `GATEWAY` claim. The terminal matrix (E3) and the install matrix (E2) can run in parallel with gateway runs. |

## 8. Independence constraints

- The held-out task author must not see Nexus source, the development tasks or tuning history. It runs in a separate session with only the task schema and external repositories. Its output is sealed by a sha256 manifest committed before RC1.
- The independent reviewer in ACCEPTANCE §8 must not be the agent or session that implemented the slices under review.
- An implementing agent never edits `eval/heldout-manifest.json`, scorer thresholds or ACCEPTANCE §6.4 after the freeze.

```sh
else
```

| Resource | Rule |
|---|---|
| Source | One `git worktree` per claimed slice: `git worktree add ../nexus-wt/<slice> -b v1/<plan>-<slice> origin/main`. Never edit `~/nexus-code` itself. It is the owner's checkout, and `/usr/local/bin/nexus` runs from it. |
| Branch | `v1/plan-NN-pr-Nx`. One branch per slice. Never commit to `main` directly. |
| HOME and state | Until PLAN-08 PR-8a lands, every test, build and probe run sets `HOME=$(mktemp -d)` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$HOME/.config"`. After PR-8a, the test setup enforces this, but scripts and probes outside `npm test` must still set it. **Never** run anything that writes to the real `~/.nexus` or `~/.config/nexus`. |
| Test runs | Full suites run on a **snapshot copy** of the worktree (`git worktree add` at the commit under test, or `git archive`), never on the tree being edited. `tsx` reads `src/` live. |
| Builds | Each worktree builds into its own `core/target`, and `cli/dist` is per worktree. To share the Rust build cache, set `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` per worktree, never to one shared directory. |
| Ports | Mock servers bind `127.0.0.1:0` (an ephemeral port) and publish the chosen port to a file. Fixed ports are forbidden. |
| Processes | Kill only PIDs you started, taken from `$!` or `ps -eo pid,args \| grep -v grep`. **Never `pkill -f` or `killall`.** Long background jobs are stopped through the agent's own task controls. |
| Full test suites | The PTY and provider tests are timing-sensitive. Take the claim `SUITE` before running a full suite (`make test`, or `npm test` over all files). While anyone holds `SUITE`, nobody runs other suites or targeted test files on the same machine. Concurrent load caused a false failure on 2026-10-15: `cloud_providers` saw an extra provider request after a load-induced timeout. Release the claim when the run ends. |
| Inference | There is one inference host (DEC-16). Any run that uses the gateway takes the claim `GATEWAY` first. That includes eval runs, live checks and stripped-proxy runs. One gateway run at a time, which keeps eval timings valid and prevents overload. Small cloud checks (E5) take `CLOUD` to avoid duplicate spend. |
| Credentials | Agents never read or copy `~/.config/nexus/credentials.json`, `config.env` values, or gateway tokens. The stripped proxy reads the token file itself. |

These files are touched by several plans. An agent editing one must hold its `FILE_` claim for the **shortest** period: edit, test, push, merge, then release.

| `cli/src/agent.ts` | 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 11 | Claim required. Keep each change local to the line ranges the plan names. Rebase immediately before merge and re-run that slice's tests on the rebased snapshot. |
| `cli/src/index.ts` | 01, 03, 04, 06, 08, 10, 11 | Claim required. **PLAN-06 PR-6b (unified launcher) lands first.** Other plans add commands and flags afterwards. |
| `cli/src/tools.ts` | 01, 02, 03, 06, 11 | Claim required. **PLAN-02 PR-2b (signal plumbing) lands before PLAN-03 PR-3c (`safeFetch`)**. |
| `cli/src/sidecar.ts` | 01, 02, 03, 05, 08 | Claim required |
| `cli/src/doctor.ts` | 01, 03, 05, 06, 08 | Claim required. Each plan adds **new check functions** in separate blocks. Only PLAN-06 PR-6d changes existing checks. |
| `cli/src/client.ts` | 03, 05, 08, 11 | Claim required. **PLAN-03 PR-3a (env layering) lands before any PLAN-05 slice.** |
| `cli/src/repl.ts` | 01, 05, 08 | Claim required |

### Ledger updates (`docs/v1.0.0/REQUIREMENTS.md`)

A slice changes only the rows for its own requirement IDs: the status, test-reference and evidence cells, in place. It never reorders, adds or removes rows, and never edits another slice's rows. New requirements discovered during work go to §6, not into the ledger. Because rows are independent lines, git merges these edits cleanly. If a conflict appears anyway, resolve it row by row, keeping both changes.

## 5. Commit and merge discipline

1. Before **every** commit, compare `git rev-parse HEAD` with the commit you last made. Then run `git log <yours>..HEAD` on the branch. If anything foreign appears, stop and reconcile. Never commit generated artifacts (evidence, dist, lockfiles) over a branch that moved (lessons 2026-10-13).
2. Commits are scoped to the slice. Do not reformat or clean up files outside the boundary.
3. Merge order follows the precedence rules in §4 and the ROADMAP milestone order. Within a milestone, the slice with fewer hot-file claims merges first.
4. Rebase onto `origin/main` immediately before merging. Re-run the slice's targeted tests, plus `make test`, on a snapshot of the rebased commit. Merge only if both pass.
5. Pushing, tagging, publishing and changing GitHub state (issues, milestones, releases) are **owner-approved actions** (DECISIONS X-list). Agents prepare them and do not perform them.
6. Preserve unrelated user work: the untracked `nexus-continuity-validation/`, the stashes, and any dirty files you did not create. Never stash, reset, clean or check out over them.

| Record | Where | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Claims | `$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/nexus-claims/` | Who owns which slice or file right now |
| Claim log | `$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/nexus-claims.log` (append-only, one line per event) | Claim, release, broken claim, boundary request |
| Boundary requests and discovered requirements | The PR description, under the heading `Needs from other slices`. Mirrored as one line in the claim log. | So the owning slice's agent can pick it up. Never fixed silently out of scope. |
| Slice evidence | `docs/reviews/evidence/v1/<plan>-<slice>/` (new directory per slice) | No shared evidence files, so agents cannot overwrite each other's evidence |

## 7. Safe parallel lanes

The following groupings can run at the same time with no hot-file contention beyond §4 claims. They are listed by milestone.

| Phase | Parallel lanes |
|---|---|
| M0 | (a) PLAN-08 PR-8a, which must merge first. Then in parallel: (b) PLAN-06 PR-6a, (c) PLAN-09 PR-9a. |
| M1 | (a) PLAN-01 PR-1a → PR-1b → PR-1c (sequential, owns `capabilities.ts`, `agent.ts` dispatch). (b) PLAN-02 PR-2a (Rust only). (c) PLAN-03 PR-3a → PR-3b (config/egress). (d) PLAN-11 PR-11a (`parser.ts`) and PR-11b (`tester.ts`, after PR-1c). Lanes (b), (c) and (d) do not touch `capabilities.ts`. |
| M2 (alongside M1) | (a) PLAN-07 PR-7a/7b/7c (workflows, scripts). (b) PLAN-06 PR-6b after PLAN-01 PR-1b (shares `index.ts` flags). |
| M3 | (a) PLAN-04 (`agent.ts` turn, operation runner). (b) PLAN-05 (`client.ts`, provider modules). (c) PLAN-10 harness (`eval/`, no product files). (d) Held-out task authoring by the agent author, **outside the repository**: no access to Nexus source or the development set (DEC-05). |
| M4 (alongside M3) | PLAN-08 PR-8b..8e. Coordinate with PLAN-04 on `state.ts` through `FILE_` claims. |
| M5 | **Serial on `GATEWAY`.** The eval runner, the stripped-proxy runs and the independent reviewer's live task each take the `GATEWAY` claim. The terminal matrix (E3) and the install matrix (E2) can run in parallel with gateway runs. |

## 8. Independence constraints

- The held-out task author must not see Nexus source, the development tasks or tuning history. It runs in a separate session with only the task schema and external repositories. Its output is sealed by a sha256 manifest committed before RC1.
- The independent reviewer in ACCEPTANCE §8 must not be the agent or session that implemented the slices under review.
- An implementing agent never edits `eval/heldout-manifest.json`, scorer thresholds or ACCEPTANCE §6.4 after the freeze.

# Nexus Code v1.2.1 plan

Status: PLAN, written 2026-11-15 against `main` plus the v1.2.0-rc.1 notes. Evidence and the full gap register are in [`GAP_ANALYSIS.md`](GAP_ANALYSIS.md); gap ids (GA-nn) refer to it. Owner decisions are recorded in section 6 (answered 2026-11-15) and nothing marked "decision" starts without one.

## 1. Purpose and theme

v1.2.0 made "done" mean something (independent verification, typed requirements, guarded verification files, convergence stopping, receipts with real dependencies) and said plainly that none of it is independent qualification. v1.2.1 is about **measuring it, shipping it to more people, containing it by default, and hardening what shipped**:

1. **Measure** the core claim (fewer false completions) on public benchmarks and on real projects.
2. **Reach**: platforms and integration points peers already have.
3. **Contain** by default, and close the record-only gaps.
4. **Harden** weak-model handling and context.
5. **Pay down** the process and maintainability debt that made v1.2.0 take a week of CI.

Non-goals: new verification features beyond the deferred SI-5/DV-3/DV-4 set, new providers, a hosted product, any claim of frontier-grade.

## 2. Rules for this release

- Every unit is test-first, one PR, with local Code / Security / Slop reviews on the exact head before merge (prompts: `memory/entire-agent-review-prompts.md`), required CI green at the exact head, and honest framing in notes: "ledger closed, qualification pending" until an external result exists.
- No new runtime dependency without an owner decision. No change to tags (immutable). Dependabot PRs roll in.
- A behaviour change that can break an existing user (containment default, concurrency validation, shell-write hard stop) is a decision (section 6), a release-notes line, and an opt-out.
- A unit that finds the plan wrong says so in its PR and updates this file.
- Live inference is the project's gateway only; any live measurement holds the `GATEWAY` claim and uses the key from the environment, never printed.

## 3. Release gates

v1.2.1 ships when:

| Gate | Condition |
|---|---|
| G-1 | `make test` green at the exact head; required CI green on the release commit; main CI green on the merge commit |
| G-2 | Every P0 unit merged; every P1 unit merged or carries a dated owner deferral |
| G-3 | Live-gateway tool-call matrix (G1.1-4) repeated on the release-candidate archive and recorded as evidence (also closes GA-03 for v1.2.0 if still open) |
| G-4 | A first external-style measurement exists and is published in the notes with its limits (MQ-2): at minimum a pinned Terminal-Bench subset run through the Harbor adapter, with the false-completion rate reported beside the pass rate. If no run is possible in the window, the notes say "no external measurement" and the release is still allowed; the framing never changes |
| G-5 | No test in the suite can leak a bridge, agent, gateway, child process or timer past its file (PC-2 guard green) |
| G-6 | Docs: README, CHANGELOG, manual and examples current (DH-1…DH-3) |

"Externally qualified" is defined in section 7 so the word has one meaning.

## 4. Workstreams and units

Size: S = one PR; M = two to four PRs; L = a program. P0 = must-have, P1 = should-have, P2 = stretch (may roll to v1.2.2).

### MQ: measure and qualify

| Unit | What | Accept | Size | Pri |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MQ-0 | Run the G1.1-4 matrix on the v1.2.0 release-candidate archive under the GATEWAY claim; record `docs/evidence/v1.2.0/…` and add the figure to the rc notes (closes GA-03) | evidence file with archive sha256, per-alias counts, repaired / invalid counts; notes updated by a docs PR | S | P0 |
| MQ-1 | Benchmark adapter: a Harbor / Terminal-Bench runner for Nexus (template: Goose `evals/harbor/`), plus a SWE-bench-style adapter if the task format allows a hermetic run | `nexus` runs a pinned subset in task containers with no network leaks; results JSON with task ids, model, gateway alias, Nexus version, seed or sampling, wall time, and the raw verdicts (VERIFIED / REGRESSION_FREE / UNVERIFIED / BLOCKED) | M | P0 |
| MQ-2 | False-completion metric: for every run record Nexus's own verdict and the benchmark's ground truth; report pass rate, **claimed-done-but-wrong rate**, and **verified-but-wrong rate** with Wilson 95% intervals (the repo already has the interval code in `eval/score.mjs`); compare against the same model through at least one peer harness already adapted in `eval/configs/pilot-*.json` | a report where a false VERIFIED is named and explained; the notes state the sample size and that it is self-run | M | P0 |
| MQ-3 | Real-project smoke: a nightly job that runs a scripted task on pinned copies of representative repositories (a JS project with `node_modules`, a Makefile project, a Python project, a Rust project, and the owner's own repositories where licensing allows) and fails when `task_completed` errors, hangs or ends UNVERIFIED for an avoidable reason. This is the test that would have caught the v1.1.4 every-completion error before release | job red on a seeded regression (a repo whose verifier cannot be bound must complete as REGRESSION_FREE) | M | P0 |
| MQ-4 | Scheduled model conformance: a nightly or weekly job that runs the tool-call matrix against the configured gateway aliases and alerts on a drop; claim protocol so it never collides with a human run (template: Goose `model-toolcall-conformance.yml`) | one alert path tested with a forced failure | S | P1 |
| MQ-5 | CERI baseline identity bound to evidence (audit F02): baseline manifest, model digest, sampling and configuration recorded and verified when a comparison is made; a comparison without bound baselines is labelled non-certifying (decision D7, included) | a comparison against an edited baseline fails; test with a swapped manifest | M | P0 |
| MQ-6 | CERI evidence loading verifies the integrity record (audit F06): `passed:"false"` no longer loads as true, run-id collisions are refused, a tampered record is rejected (D7) | tests for each of the three defects | M | P0 |
| MQ-7 | Audit Slices B–G, decide each as a unit or a dated deferral, then build in this order: B evidence lifecycle, C verified baselines and paired comparisons (needed for MQ-2 to be called certifying), E request-context manifests, D installed-evaluator adapter, F recovery reference checker, G bounded campaigns (D7). B and C are P1; D, E, F, G are P2 and may roll | each slice either merged with tests or carries a dated deferral in this file | L | P1/P2 |
| MQ-8 | Long-horizon and A/B measurement (the Anthropic trends report, trend 3; `agent-rules-books` and the context-management post both report gains without a methodology): one multi-hour scripted task on a pinned repository with a resume part-way, and paired runs of the same scenarios with an instruction file, or tool-output clearing, on and off; report completion, claimed-done-but-wrong rate, tokens and wall time with Wilson 95% intervals | results JSON with the paired runs, model, gateway alias, Nexus version and seeds; no effect claimed unless the interval excludes zero (needs MQ-1 and MQ-2) | M | P2 (v1.2.2) |

Dependencies: MQ-1 → MQ-2 → MQ-8. MQ-3 and MQ-4 are independent. Decision D3 (what is published) and D4 (scope and cost) gate MQ-1 and MQ-2.

### VC: verification completeness (the v1.2.0 deferrals)

# Nexus Code v1.3 plan: the platform track

Status: PLAN, written 2026-11-15 against `main` plus the v1.2.0-rc.1 notes, at the owner's request ("draft the v1.3 platform track as recommended"). It follows v1.2.1 and v1.2.2 ([`docs/v1.2.1/PLAN.md`](../v1.2.1/PLAN.md), decision D12). Nothing here is a claim that Nexus Code is frontier-grade, and no unit starts without the decisions in section 7.

## 1. Purpose and theme

Frontier clients are platforms: a CLI plus a desktop app, IDE integration, background and scheduled agents, an SDK or managed API, installable plugin bundles, and enterprise policy (web sources of 2026-11-15, mostly third-party; see [`docs/v1.2.1/GAP_ANALYSIS.md`](../v1.2.1/GAP_ANALYSIS.md) §2). Nexus is a single-binary Linux CLI and TUI. It cannot match breadth or first-party model fit, and a worse copy of three funded platforms is not a goal.

The v1.3 theme: **let other programs drive Nexus and let teams govern it, without weakening the gate.** Every new surface (an IDE over ACP, a scheduler, a hook, a plugin, an SDK caller, a managed policy) goes through the same approval and verification gates as the terminal does. The differentiator to build on is the one nobody else ships by default: a completion you can audit (independent verification, receipts, evidence). Two consequences shape the plan:

1. **Nexus as the verification layer for other harnesses.** `nexus verify` and an MCP/ACP `verify` tool let a Codex, Claude Code or Aider session ask Nexus to independently check its work. This costs little (the machinery exists) and is positioned where the platforms are weakest.
2. **Governance as a product.** Managed policy with fixed precedence, a hash-chained and optionally signed audit export, and hooks that can only tighten.

Non-goals: a marketplace, a desktop or mobile app, a Nexus-specific VS Code extension (ACP clients already exist), hosted or multi-tenant operation (dropped 2026-11-15, decision D8), plugin auto-update, any new runtime dependency without a decision.

## 2. Evidence and its limits

- **Nexus today** (read-only inventory, 2026-11-15; "present" means present in source or docs, nothing was run): sidecar/TUI protocol is NDJSON over the sidecar's stdio with `PROTOCOL_VERSION = 1`, an event `v`, a one-way `hello`, typed unions in `cli/src/protocol.ts:53-204` hand-mirrored in `core/src/bin/nexus_tui/protocol.rs`, **no schema file, no socket**; `nexus run --json` returns `TaskExecutionResult` (`cli/src/core/app.ts:44`) with no schema or version, exit codes defined only in code (0 verified, 2 completed-unverified, 130 interrupted, 1 otherwise); `ApplicationCore` is an accidental re-export (`cli/src/index.ts:1240`) and `cli/package.json` has `main` and `bin` but no `exports` or `types`; operations are durable and resumable (per-operation lock, 12 h wait survives restart, `maxConcurrentUnits` capped at 64 and clamped to 1 without `git.isolate`) but **foreground-only**, with no scheduler, cron, trigger or daemon in the code; plugins are plain JS modules with no manifest, checksum or install command, workspace plugins load after `nexus trust` with full process authority, hooks cover pre/post tool only; policy is the workspace-local `.nexus-security.json`, **fails open to defaults on a parse error**, with no system or admin layer; session export is `nexus-session-export/2` reachable only through `/export`; the flight log is append-only by convention (no hash chain found) and the CERI evidence store hashes files but has no signature or verify command; local OTLP-style traces are written on every session with no opt-in gate and no network exporter found; a goal (objective ledger) persists across sessions via `--resume`, but nothing re-launches a task on its own.
- **Peers, read from source** (shallow clones of 2026-11-13/14; Codex at commit 336b19a; untrusted code, nothing run): ACP servers in goose (`crates/goose/src/acp`), Cline (`apps/cli/src/acp/acpAgent.ts`), Gemini CLI (`packages/cli/src/acp`) and opencode (`packages/cli/src/acp/agent.ts`), the Codex `app-server` (JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio, websocket or UDS; schema generated from Rust types and checked in); schedulers in goose (`scheduler/full.rs`), Cline (`*.cron.md` and event specs) and opencode (a `ScheduleTable` with `in`/`at`/`every`/`cron` and an optional deterministic wake `check`); hooks in Gemini CLI (`docs/hooks/reference.md`), goose (`hooks/mod.rs`), Cline and Codex; extension manifests in Gemini CLI (`gemini-extension.json`), goose (Open Plugins and Gemini formats) and opencode; policy tiers in Gemini CLI (`core/src/policy/config.ts:67-71`), opencode (`managed-policy.ts`) and Codex (`requirements.toml`); goal state in opencode (`schema/src/goal.ts`) and Codex (`thread/goal/*`).
- **XERJ reference queries** (2026-11-15, local node, read-only; the `opencode` index is flagged "not verified complete", so a miss there is not proof of absence): `xerj code opencode` for ACP, scheduling and plugin manifests; `xerj search --prefix goose` for ACP, scheduler and extension manifests; `xerj search --prefix xc-opencode` for managed policy. **Took:** opencode's wire-level ACP fixture pattern (`packages/cli/test/acp/wire-fixture.ts`) for protocol conformance tests; opencode's schedule model (`schema/src/schedule.ts`, `core/src/schedule/sql.ts`: `next_due_at`, `remaining_runs`, `last_outcome`, deterministic wake check with hard limits) and its documented GitHub scheduled-workflow example; goose's cron-on-a-recipe scheduler shape (`scheduler/full.rs`, `commands/schedule.rs`); goose's checked-in ACP schema and method metadata (`acp-meta.json`); goose's plugin formats (`plugins/formats/gemini.rs`, `open_plugins.rs`); opencode's managed policy as config statements with an action, a resource and an effect (`config/plugin/policy.ts`). **Rejected:** opencode's in-process Effect plugin hooks (a JS-in-process model is what Nexus is trying to move away from), goose's per-run `Auto` mode for scheduled runs (unattended runs must never get allow-always), and any code copied verbatim: reference code is read-only inspiration.
- **Research notes** (2026-11-15): the Anthropic 2026 agentic coding trends report (read in full; a vendor document with no methodology, customer-reported figures) and OpenHands (documentation, not source) support three priorities here: VR-1 and VR-2 (the report's own evidence is that people delegate what is cheaply checkable, so verifiability is the delegation boundary), PA-1 (it names a view of concurrent agent sessions) and AC-1 (above). They are framing, not evidence about Nexus.
- **Not covered:** Claude Code and agy were not read (web sources only); parts of Cline's daemon, Codex's hook handler types and plugin manifest, and goose's managed policy were sampled, not read in full; peer behaviour under load was not measured.

## 3. Principles

1. **Protocol first.** Nothing else in this plan is safe to build until the client protocol is published, schema'd, versioned and conformance-tested.
2. **One gate.** A new surface can request an approval but can never answer one on behalf of Nexus's own gates (SI-2, CS-* rules, verification). A client that answers "allow" to a denied action must have no effect; this is tested.
3. **Tighten only.** Hooks and managed policy may deny, require a human, or rewrite arguments toward safer values. They never grant.
4. **Unattended means stricter.** Scheduled and detached runs never get allow-always, run in a fresh worktree, and record that they were unattended in every receipt.
5. **Explicit trust.** Project-defined hooks, plugins and policy run only after a trust decision keyed by a content hash; a changed file asks again.
6. **Schemas come from types.** Generate JSON Schema from the TypeScript types and check it in with a parity test, so the Rust mirror cannot drift (reference: Codex `app-server-protocol` schema export, goose `acp-schema.json`).
7. **No new runtime dependency** without a decision. ACP is plain JSON-RPC; hash chains and ed25519 signing use `node:crypto`.
8. **Experimental is a flag.** New methods sit behind `experimental` at `initialize` (reference: Codex `experimentalApi`) until a conformance suite has run against two real clients.

## 4. Workstreams and units

Size: S = one PR; M = two to four PRs; L = a program. P0 = prerequisite, P1 = core, P2 = stretch.

### PF: protocol and embedding foundation

| Unit | What | Accept | Size | Pri |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PF-1 | Publish the client protocol: JSON Schema generated from `cli/src/protocol.ts`, a checked-in copy, a TS/Rust parity test replacing hand-sync, capability negotiation in `hello` / `initialize` (version range, `experimental` flag), `docs/PROTOCOL.md`; wire-level conformance fixtures (reference: opencode `packages/cli/test/acp/wire-fixture.ts`) | schema diff fails CI when a type changes without a version decision; a recorded session replays through the fixture harness | M | P0 |
| PF-2 | `nexus run --json` result schema with a `schema_version`, documented exit codes in the manual, `--input-json` or stdin for the task | schema validated in tests; a consumer test parses the output | S | P0 |
| PF-3 | Transport beyond a parent's stdio: a unix domain socket (default) with a token and origin check for any localhost HTTP/WebSocket listener (reference: goose `acp/transport/auth.rs`, constant-time compare); several clients may attach and reattach | a second client attaches to a running session; a wrong token is refused; the socket is mode 0600 | M | P1 |
| PF-4 | Library entry point: a `lib` entry that does not run commander on import, `exports` and `types` in `cli/package.json`, a package name decision, a documented minimal embedding example that spawns the sidecar | an example script runs a verified task through the entry point in CI | M | P1 |

### AC: ACP and IDE access

| Unit | What | Accept | Size | Pri |

## 3. Authority model (decision, not new machinery)

Requirement and invariant authority is the field the ledger already has: operator text is authoritative and immutable by agents; anything an agent proposes is recorded as inferred and never gates. Repository content (docs, comments, config) is evidence, never instruction, unless the operator elevates it with an explicit command. Architectural invariants are authoritative only when declared by the operator or in a committed, operator-owned rules file; a repository's current structure is observed, not intended. Measurements (new dependency, new abstraction) stay advisory unless they violate a declared invariant.

## 3. Authority model (decision, not new machinery)

Requirement and invariant authority is the field the ledger already has: operator text is authoritative and immutable by agents; anything an agent proposes is recorded as inferred and never gates. Repository content (docs, comments, config) is evidence, never instruction, unless the operator elevates it with an explicit command. Architectural invariants are authoritative only when declared by the operator or in a committed, operator-owned rules file; a repository's current structure is observed, not intended. Measurements (new dependency, new abstraction) stay advisory unless they violate a declared invariant.

| Unit | What | Accept | Size | Pri |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| VC-1 | SI-5 operator-declared boundary rules (import allow/deny, protected public files) checked on the candidate diff with deterministic analysis; interface/schema/format changes classified compatible / potentially breaking / unknown; coverage limits always reported | boundary violation = REJECT; undeclared dependency = advisory; unknown coverage disclosed; rules absent = no behaviour change; CERI `cumulative-chan
| VC-2 | DV-3 operator-authorised regression obligations: a confirmed failing test becomes a protected obligation only on operator authorisation; the original failure record is kept when later minimised | authorised obligation replayed on the next candidate and a weakening edit recorded; unauthorised promotion cannot happen | M | P2 |
| VC-3 | DV-4 attempt lineage (parent attempt, diff hash) and behavioural differential against a declared reference only when an authorised requirement names one (the Anthropic 2026 trends report's flagship long run, Rakuten's seven-hour single run at 99.9% numerical accuracy against a reference method, succeeded because a reference existed: the reference is what lets a long run stay autonomous. Raising this to P1 if
| VC-4 | Close the two pending CERI scenarios once VC-1 lands; assign an owner to every scenario in `semantic_integrity` | pending count 0 or each pending carries a unit id | S | P1 |
| VC-5 | Re-check `verified` on resume (invalidate when the candidate identity differs) and persist the unbound-pass marker so a resumed task does not hit the "no matching baseline" refusal | resume test: edited workspace demotes `verified`; resume after an unbound pass completes as REGRESSION_FREE | S | P1 |
| VC-6 | Type-check gaps: baseline run to catch callers broken in untouched files, count shell-changed files as modified (workspace diff, not edit tools), Go (`go vet`) and Python (pyright/mypy when configured) | a change that breaks an untouched caller blocks VERIFIED; opt-out stays | M | P2 |
| VC-7 | Convergence on the `run_tests` path and for operator-configured verifiers | a `run_tests`-only loop stops with the history attached | S | P2 |
| VC-8 | Per-role tool allowlists beyond reviewer and researcher (old backlog REQ:259, accepted 2026-11-15): allowlists for implementer and tester, consistent with SI-2's tester scoping (`roleToolAllowList`, `cli/src/agent.ts:5490`) | each role's disallowed tool is refused with a reason; existing flows unchanged | S | P2 (v1.2.2) |
| VC-9 | Headless needs-input audit (Anthropic 2026 trends report, trend 4: agents that learn when to ask for help): list every path where a headless run needs an operator decision (steering that negates a requirement, a requirement marked blocked, a denied approval, a verification-file edit) and give each the same resumable outcome, a stable `needs_input` reason carrying the question and resumable with the answer; b
| VC-10 | Steering semantic judge (optional; evidence in `docs/research/steering-judgment/`): a judge provider interface (none by default, the configured gateway, or an explicit opt-in third party) asked, for each live requirement, whether the steering message withdraws, defers or changes it; conflict (the existing operator decision) if the regex hits or `withdraws` >= 0.7 whatever `defers` says, advisory note betwee

| PR-2 | Data-driven provider registry: a `ProviderDef` schema (id, label, protocol, base URL template with validated variables such as `{resource}`, query, headers, auth kind `bearer`/`header`/`none`, env names, model source, capability defaults, `omitParams`, `streamOnly`); the six existing ids become table entries; the Copilot gpt-5 protocol rule and ChatGPT parameter omission become data; a user file `~/.config/nexus/providers.json` (operator-only; a project-level file is refused, like `NEXU
| PR-3 | models.dev snapshot: an offline generator script turns the models.dev data into `cli/src/providers.generated.ts` (provider ids, base URLs and env names for the OpenAI-compatible set; per-model context, output, tool-choice modes, reasoning effort, cache and price), dated and schema-validated, with no runtime network fetch; an explicit `nexus models refresh` writes a local cache that overrides the snapshot | table validates in CI; the snapshot date is shown by `nexus providers`; the cache
| PR-4 | Capability-aware behaviour from that data: use `capabilities.tools.choice` before forcing `tool_choice: required` in the content-form re-ask (a model that lists only `auto` and `none` gets the corrective note instead of a request error), use per-model context and output limits instead of the 65,536 default, offer the model's reasoning effort levels | a mock model that rejects forced tool use does not receive `required`; context limit resolves from the snapshot; G1.1-4 matrix (WM-3) unch

### PC: process and CI

| Unit | What | Accept | Size | Pri |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PC-1 | CI wall time: run `linux-x86_64` in parallel with `test-matrix` where its work does not need it, split the CLI suite into shards, cache toolchains; update the stale "12–20 minutes" comment (decision D10: required check names and runner minutes) | median PR CI under 40 minutes with the sam
| PC-2 | Leak and hang guard: a shared test helper that registers bridges, agents, gateways and child processes and fails the file at teardown if any survive; a per-file timeout in `run_tests.mjs`; a rule that lists test files constructing a bridge or agent without it (2 found, names to be captured 
| PC-3 | Flake budget: record rerun-on-failure events, report weekly, fail when a test needs reruns twice in 20 runs | report committed as an artifact | S | P1 |
| PC-4 | Cross-runner reproducibility (22.04 vs 24.04) as a scheduled job, not a manual dispatch | job green; alert on drift | S | P2 |
| PC-5 | Opt-in crash and error reporting: confirm what OTLP does today (opt-in status unverified), document it, add a local crash report file under `~/.nexus/` | doc plus a test that nothing leaves the host without opt-in | S | P2 (settled by v1.3 GV-4; see docs/v1.3.0/PLAN.md) |
| PC-6 | Dependency hygiene: `commander` major bump if safe, review the two Dependabot PRs, keep the no-deprecated gate | gate green | S | P2 |

### MT: maintainability

## 5. Sequencing and release split

Capacity warning. After the 2026-11-15 decisions the unit list is about three times what v1.2.0 carried, and v1.2.0 took a week of agent work with a 70-minute CI cycle. All of it cannot be one release without cutting corners that this project does not cut. Decision D12 (accepted 2026-11-15): **v1.2.1 = Phase 0 + Phase 1 + Phase 2; v1.2.2 = Phase 3 and the native provider protocols.** Anything not merged with green gates rolls with a dated note in this file; a unit is never half-merged to hit a d

Phase 0 (immediately after v1.2.0 ships): MQ-0, DH-1, DH-2, DH-5, PC-2, PC-1. These cut the cycle time, remove the hang class and finish the evidence.

Phase 1 (independent, parallelisable): MQ-3, MQ-5, MQ-6, MQ-1, then MQ-2 (needs MQ-5/MQ-6 to be called certifying); PR-1, PR-2, PR-3, PR-9, PR-11; CS-3, CS-4, WM-1, WM-2, WM-4, CX-1, CX-5, VC-5.

Phase 2: PR-4, PR-5, PR-12; CS-7, CS-8 (D5); MQ-7 slices B and C; CS-1 and CS-2 (defaults per D1 and D2: CS-1 stays opt-in unless the default is changed by a later decision); CX-2, CX-3, VC-1, RD-3, RD-4, MT-3, WM-3, MQ-4, PC-3, DH-3, DH-4, DH-6, CX-7, CS-11, VC-9, PC-7.

Phase 3 (v1.2.2): native protocols PR-6 (Gemini), PR-7 (Bedrock), PR-8 (Vertex), PR-10; CS-9, CS-10, VC-8, RD-7 (added 2026-11-15 from the old-backlog review); MQ-7 slices D, E, F, G; RD-1 (macOS arm64; D6 default is Linux x86_64 only, so this waits for a decision), MT-1, MT-2, VC-2, VC-3, VC-6, VC-7, CX-4, CX-6, RD-2, RD-5, RD-6, CS-5, CS-6, PC-4, PC-5, PC-6, MQ-8 (needs MQ-1 and MQ-2), VC-10 (gated on a larger evaluation).

D9 note: "every cloud provider configurable" is delivered in v1.2.1 for every OpenAI-compatible provider and for Azure OpenAI, Gemini's compatible endpoint and Bedrock's OpenAI-compatible endpoint (PR-2, PR-3, PR-5), which is most of the 334 providers in models.dev. The three native protocols (Gemini, Bedrock Converse with SigV4, Vertex with ADC) are the largest pieces and ship in v1.2.2 unless you move them up.

## 3. Lifecycle

One model for durable autonomous work, defined in `core/operation.ts` (header) and used by `nexus operation` and
`/team`:

| Unit state | Meaning |
|---|---|
| RUNNABLE | dependencies COMPLETE; waiting for the scheduler |
| RUNNING | a turn is executing on its assigned resource |
| PARKED | a qualified resource will be eligible again at a known time; no model context is held |
| WAITING_ON_DEPENDENCY | some dependency is not COMPLETE (a BLOCKED dependency keeps it here) |
| COMPLETE | the turn completed with an established result: `turnSucceeded(TurnResult)`, the same predicate as `nexus run` exit 0 (outcome `VERIFIED`, or `NOT_REQUIRED`). `UNVERIFIED` work is not complete |
| BLOCKED | no safe autonomous transition; carries one structured decision |

| Operation state | Meaning |
|---|---|
| RUNNING | some unit is runnable or running (the "active" state) |
| WAITING | nothing can run now; required work is parked on a known time |
| BLOCKED | nothing can run or wait; required work needs a decision |
| COMPLETE | every required unit is COMPLETE |
| CANCELLED | the operator stopped it; history preserved |

There is no FAILED state. Terminal execution failure (provider rejection, step limit, unknown execution with its
replay budget spent, interrupted tool, no qualified resource) is BLOCKED with a decision; environmental conditions
(rate limit, capacity, transport outage) park or reroute. `TurnResult` remains the per-turn vocabulary; the unit
state is derived from it in `AgentWorkUnitExecutor.classify`, so no second set of execution enums exists. A turn
that completed without an established result (`UNVERIFIED`: verification not run, no applicable verifier, or
`CONTEXT_EVIDENCE_NOT_RETAINED`) is BLOCKED with a retry/revise decision, never COMPLETE.

`NOT_REQUIRED` means the turn changed nothing *and* every tool output it relied on was still in its context. When
context compaction removes a tool observation (elided or truncated by the detail budget) and the turn does not run
that tool with the same arguments again, the turn is `UNVERIFIED` with reason `CONTEXT_EVIDENCE_NOT_RETAINED`. The
durable record tells the model exactly which outputs left its context (`Output no longer in context (rerun to see it

re-derives what it no longer holds from its recovered conversation. Removal tracking is per turn (plus resumed
conversations); an interactive REPL turn relying on output compacted away in an earlier turn is not flagged.

### Decisions

A BLOCKED unit carries `{ id: "<unit>#<n>", cause, question, options[] }`. Every option is a typed `DecisionAction`:
`retry` (optionally clearing operator-needed resource conditions), `keep_waiting`, `assign` (to a named resource,
listing the requirements it overrides — never independence or trust), `revise` (operator note appended to the unit's
task), `drop` (advisory units only) and `cancel_operation`. `ConvergenceScheduler.resolve` validates the decision id,
the option id and the action against current state and throws `DecisionRejected` otherwise; applying one records
it on `unit.decisions`, emits `DECISION_APPLIED` and resumes the operation under the driver lock. Operators apply
them with `nexus operation decide <operation> <decision> <option> [--note …] [--no-resume]`. Nothing else mutates a
BLOCKED unit.

`nexus operation decide` reports a rejected choice as `Decision rejected: …` on stderr and exits with status `2`.

operation state. Run `nexus operation status <operation> --json`; the result is a one-element array. Inspect
`$[0].units[].blocked.decision` and `$[0].blocked.decisions` for the current decision IDs, questions, and offered
option IDs. The human-readable status view

state. Do not reuse an option from an older status display: decisions can become stale after another operator action
or after the operation changes state.

The CLI rejects a decision when the operation is already complete or cancelled, the decision ID is no longer
pending, or the option ID is not one currently offered. It also rejects actions that would violate the operation's
contract: `revise` requires `--note`, a required unit cannot be dropped, and `assign` must name a configured resource
that satisfies the unit's minimum trust boundary. Trust requirements cannot be overridden by an operator decision.


The option number above is illustrative; use the ID shown by `status` for the current operation. The command resumes
the operation after a valid decision unless `--no-resume` is supplied. With `--no-resume`, Nexus records the valid
decision and prints the updated status without starting the operation again.

## 9. Restart and reboot

Process restart: proven. Operation state and each unit's task conversation are durable; a driver killed at any
point leaves a lock whose pid is dead, which the next `nexus operation resume` takes over; interrupted RUNNING units
are reconciled (bounded unknown-outcome resumes).

Host reboot: Nexus has no daemon or service lifecycle (the only long-lived child is the per-process Rust RPC
helper), so none was added. After a reboot the state is intact and a lock written before boot is treated as stale
even if its pid number has been reused (`OperationStore.acquire` compares the lock time with boot time). The
smallest integration point is an OS boot hook that runs `nexus operation resume` (with no id it resumes the latest
WAITING or RUNNING operation for the workspace; BLOCKED operations are excluded because they need a decision), e.g.

```
# Lessons

- 2026-10-12 — Concurrent edits in the checkout after a rate-limit pause may come from an agent the operator started
  to continue *my* work, not from an unrelated actor. Before treating them as foreign (splitting them off, excluding
  them from commits), ask whether a continuation agent was used and read its summary; then fold its work into the
  plan and verify it like my own.
- 2026-10-13 — Another agent (Cursor) committed to the same branch while I worked; my evidence commit then replaced its
  newer evidence. A clean `git status` is not enough: before every commit, check `git log -1` against the commit I last
  made (and `git log ORIG..HEAD` for foreign commits); if HEAD moved, stop and reconcile — never commit generated
  artefacts (evidence, dist) over a branch that moved.

## 2026-10-13 — eval harness (self-caught)
- Paths handed to a spawned agent (CA bundles, output dirs) must be absolute: the agent runs with another cwd. Resolve
  `--out` once at startup.
- Set `PWD` (and XDG dirs) explicitly for spawned tools: some take the project from an inherited `$PWD`, not the
  process cwd — OpenCode edited the task fixture this way.
- Never `pkill -f <pattern>` from a shell whose own command line contains the pattern (it kills itself); node runners
  show as `MainThread` in `comm`, so filter by PID from `ps -eo pid,args`.
- Monitor filters on outcomes: `VERIFIED` is a substring of `UNVERIFIED`; anchor (`: VERIFIED `).
- Run a smoke pass of every adapter with the exact runner invocation (relative paths included) before scored runs.

## 2026-10-13 — compaction/continuity session
- Repeated the `pkill -f <pattern>` self-kill (exit 144) despite the 2026-10-13 lesson above. Rule: never use `pkill -f`
  at all; stop background work with TaskStop, or kill by PID taken from `ps -eo pid,args` filtered with `grep -v grep`.
- HEAD of the operator's checkout moved (reset to origin/main, stash, foreign uncommitted edits) during a usage-limit
  pause. Verified what landed before acting, then worked in an isolated worktree instead of on top of edits I could not
  attribute.
- A full test run reads `src/` live (tsx): editing sources while it runs contaminates results. Run long suites on a
  snapshot copy of the tree, and keep editing the worktree.

## 2026-10-15/16 — v1 implementation with a second agent
- Running targeted test files while a full suite ran on the same machine produced a false failure (an extra provider
  request after a load-induced timeout). Rule: one test run at a time per machine; take the `SUITE` claim
  (docs/v1.0.0/CONCURRENCY.md) and leave other runs until it is released.
- During a usage-limit pause, a continuation agent took over my worktrees and branches, following the claims protocol.
  Before resuming, read `git log` on every v1 branch and the claims log, and fold that agent's work in rather than
  redoing it; never fast-forward or commit over a branch without checking who moved it.
- 2026-10-16: I ran targeted tests and live calls while another agent's `SUITE` claim was held, because I checked
  only for my own runs. Rule: check `ls $(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/nexus-claims` immediately before every test
  or live run, not only before full suites.
```

## Fault injection (T4)

A task or config may list `faults: [{ kind, atRequest }]`. The run's model proxy then injects that fault into the Nth
chat request (counted from 1):

| kind | Fault |
|---|---|
| `refuse` | The connection drops without an answer |
| `overloaded` | 503 with `Retry-After: 1` |
| `stream_cut` | The stream is cut after its first tool-call fragment |
| `truncate` | `finish_reason` becomes `length` |
| `context_overflow` | llama.cpp's HTTP 400 `exceed_context_size_error` |
| `malformed_tool_json` | The first tool call's arguments are no longer valid JSON |

What was injected is recorded in `model.faultsInjected`. Such runs are never treated as infrastructure reruns.
`score.mjs` reports, per fault kind:

- runs;
- **truthful** (the run ended with its own result, did not hang past its budget, and never claimed VERIFIED while the
  hidden tests failed);
- **recovered** (the hidden tests pass);
- hung past budget.

**Audit of Domain G, continuous evaluation and roadmap integration** (read-only, against `/home/mike/nexus-wt/invariants`, branch `v1/invariants-audit`, HEAD `65c76b28`, merge of #574). Nothing was run. The worktree is ahead of the main-checkout git status in your context: the log shows PR-2..5, PR-11, RD-3, DH-4 and DH-5 merged. `docs/agents/` is not in this worktree; it exists only as untracked files in the main checkout.

## 1. Eval and regression infrastructure

**Existing pieces (all paths under the worktree root):**
- **`eval/`:** an `.mjs` harness (`run.mjs`, `score.mjs`, `oracle.mjs`, `dataset.mjs`). Tasks live in `eval/datasets/core-v1/` as `examples` plus a hidden oracle with a `regression: {command}` field. There are two splits, `regression` and `benchmark`.
- **T4 fault injection:** `eval/README.md` §"Fault injection (T4)" documents a model proxy that injects a fault at a chosen request. It is a provider-side fault list, not a process-crash or side-effect fault. The kinds are `refuse`, `overloaded`, `stream_cut`, `truncate`, `context_overflow` and `malformed_tool_json`.
- **`cli/src/eval_cli.ts` and `cli/src/evaluator.ts`:** a thin launcher for versioned eval runs, and a SWE-bench-style `BenchmarkEvaluator` that records receipts. Neither is a scenario framework.
- **CERI (`cli/src/ceri/`, about 1800 lines):** `contracts.ts` defines `EvaluationDefinition` (id, version, domain, objective, fixture, budget, deterministic assertions, independent validation criteria). CERI also has `baseline.ts` and `evidence_store.ts`. `CAPABILITY_DOMAINS` already includes `semantic_integrity`.
- **The scenario format a new regression would use:** `cli/test/fixtures/ceri/semantic_integrity.scenarios.json`, with `semantic_integrity.scenarios.sha256` as its pin. Each entry has `id`, `category`, `status` (`active` or `pending`), `pendingUnit?`, `description` and `expected`.
  - The driver is `cli/test/ceri_semantic_integrity.test.ts`. Its header says expected outcomes live only in the frozen file and the drivers compute what the product does.
  - It runs scripted agent turns through `AutonomousAgent.runTurn` against the local scripted gateway helper `startGateway` in `cli/test/helpers/fixtures.ts`.
  - Currently there are 25 scenarios: 24 active and 1 pending (`cumulative-change-03`, unit SI-5).
  - **Format gap:** there are no explicit fields for initial state, trigger, invariant or evidence. They are implicit in each driver function, and `expected` is a free-form object.

**How a new regression scenario plugs in without a second framework:** add an entry to the same JSON, update the sha256 manifest, and add a driver case in `ceri_semantic_integrity.test.ts`. Alternatively add a new `CapabilityDomain` with its own fixtures file following the same pattern. Crash scenarios can reuse the child-process driver pattern from `fault_kill_mid_tool_call.test.ts`. Scenario-level fields (`state`, `trigger`, `invariant`, `evidence`) would be a schema extension, not a new framework.

**Crash, resume and recovery tests in `cli/test/`:**
- `fault_kill_mid_tool_call.test.ts`: SIGKILL during a non-idempotent tool call (SI-7, G-AI-5). It asserts the in-flight record is durable, recovery does not re-run the tool, and the operator is asked before inference resumes. It also asserts the model is told the effects are unknown and that VERIFIED is impossible afterwards.
- `durable_continuity.test.ts`: ACC-CONT-03 compaction survives SIGKILL, plus resume tests ACC-CONT-01/02/04.
- `operation_git.test.ts`: "a crash after the merge is recognised instead of merging twice".
- `operation_concurrency.test.ts`: MAO-07, restart reconciles in-flight units through the real store.
- `operation_lock.test.ts`: stale-lock takeover and a four-process race.
- `operation_runner_restart.test.ts`: explicit unit restart starts a fresh conversation.
- `suspend_resume_acceptance.test.ts` and `resume_verified_unbound.test.ts`.
- `provider_wait_resume.test.ts`, `provider_recovery*.test.ts`, `nonprogress_recovery.test.ts`, `output_truncation_recovery.test.ts` and `recover_worktree_conversation.test.ts`.
- `upgrade_transaction_recovery.test.ts` and `process_lifecycle.test.ts`.
- `helpers/compaction_crash_child.ts`, `helpers/operation_lock_child.ts` and `helpers/state_store_replacement_child.ts`.
- CERI `recovery-01`.
- Gap: I found no kill-mid-integration test beyond the post-merge case, and no side-effect idempotency test outside the one non-idempotent command.

## 2. Agent instructions and invariants

**Files:**
- `AGENTS.md` (4.1 KB, tracked) is the only substantive file. `CLAUDE.md` is 11 bytes and just contains `@AGENTS.md`.
- `.claude/settings.json`, `.codex/hooks.json`, `.cursor/hooks.json`, `.agents/hooks.json` and `.opencode/plugins/entire.ts` contain only Entire hook wiring and no invariants.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` is process only.
- `docs/agents/` (domain.md, issue-tracker.md, triage-labels.md) is untracked in the main checkout and says nothing about invariants.

**What `AGENTS.md` states:** build and test commands, XERJ reference coding, the claims protocol, and merge and release rules. It states **no architectural invariants** (state transitions, authority, side effects, provider capabilities).

**Where the invariants live:**
- `docs/EXECUTION_CONVERGENCE.md` §3 has the unit and operation state tables, the "no FAILED state" rule, "BLOCKED carries one decision" and "nothing else mutates a BLOCKED unit". It also has the `NOT_REQUIRED` meaning and the §9 restart contract.
- `docs/v1.2.0/SEMANTIC_AND_ARCHITECTURAL_INTEGRITY.md` §1 (what exists) and §3 (authority model) cover requirements, authority and acceptance.
- `docs/v1.2.0/SEMANTIC_AND_ARCHITECTURAL_INTEGRITY.md` §10 covers unknown-outcome handling and the verifier-digest re-check.

**Backed by executable tests:**
- Review ACCEPT without verifier evidence is REJECT (SI-1).
- No self-approval: `verified` needs an independent, deliverable-bound run (CERI `self-validating-*`).
- Verification-config edits are guarded (SI-2).
- Steering conflicts raise a decision (SI-3).
- Typed invariants gate completion (SI-4).
- Stale evidence invalidates `verified` (`stale-evidence-*`, `resume_verified_unbound`).
- EXECUTION_UNKNOWN blocks replay (`operation_runner_execution.ts:919`, `scheduler.ts:591`).
- Merged-but-unrecorded units are not merged twice.
- Isolation is required under concurrency (SI-8).
- Atomic state writes and quarantine of corrupt state.
- Provider capability-aware tool choice (PR-4) and the per-definition wire matrix (PR-11).

**Durable assumptions that live only in prose, comments or prompts:**
1. **Operation state transitions have no executable table.** I found no `assertTransition` or `ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS`. Status is re-derived in `ConvergenceScheduler`, and the lifecycle tables exist only in the `operation.ts` header and `EXECUTION_CONVERGENCE.md`. An illegal transition (for example BLOCKED to COMPLETE without a decision) is checked only indirectly.
2. **"Nothing else mutates a BLOCKED unit"** is enforced by `DecisionRejected` in `ConvergenceScheduler.resolve`, but I found no test that attempts each other mutation path.
3. **`reconcileInterruptedRuns` (`scheduler.ts:~618`)** sets a RUNNING unit back to RUNNABLE for up to `unknownResumeBudget` (default 2, `operation.ts:257`). It does this for any interrupted unit, regardless of whether a non-idempotent effect occurred. The kill-mid-tool test covers one command shape through the agent path. I did not verify that the replay is safe for all tool classes (write, merge, MCP, plugin).
4. **Reviewer authority.** SI-5 (G-SI-5) says `authorizedScope` is passed by no caller, and that was fixed by SI-4. Whether reviewer consensus can override a failing verifier is asserted in the doc ("not found defective") and covered by `reviewer-agreement-*`. I did not verify beyond that.
5. **Operation identity.** I found only `op-fault`-style string ids and `unit#n` decision ids. There is no content-addressed operation or action identity for side effects across restarts. `execution_tracking.test.ts` covers action identity only for loop detection, not for duplicate-effect prevention.
6. **Provider capability rules:** the model-facing rule "prose tool calls are never executed" (SI doc §10) is stated as a Nexus strength, and the wire matrix covers it. Provider-side capability negotiation and "unknown capability means don't assume" have no invariant statement.
7. **Never-claimed-in-docs-only:** the SI plan's section 3 "authority model" (operator text is authoritative, repository content is evidence only) is a decision with no single test naming it.

## 4. Build, test and claims

**Commands:**
- Setup: `make setup`. Equivalent: `npm ci --prefix cli`, then `cargo build --release --manifest-path core/Cargo.toml`, then `npm --prefix cli run build`.
- Build: `make build`. CLI build is `npm --prefix cli run build` (`tsc` + `copy_data.mjs` + `write_build_info.mjs`).
- Full tests: `make test` (cargo test, `npm --prefix cli run test:cli`, `test:scope`, `scripts/security_gates.sh`; it runs all four before failing). The CI-equivalent run is `make test-ci` and needs sudo for tmpfs mounts.
- One file: `cd cli && HOME=$(mktemp -d) node --import tsx --test test/<name>.test.ts`. `cli/scripts/run_tests.mjs` also sets a throwaway HOME and has a per-file watchdog (300 s).
- CI requires `test-matrix (22)`, `test-matrix (24)` and `linux-x86_64`.

**Node:** `engines.node >=22`. The local runtime is v24.11.1. Process or test-runner changes must run on both 22 and 24 (`AGENTS.md`).

**Claims (`docs/v1.0.0/CONCURRENCY.md`):**
- **Yes, a `SUITE` claim is required** for full suites (`make test`, or `npm test` over all files). While anyone holds it, nobody runs other suites or targeted test files on the machine. `tasks/lessons.md` (2026-10-16) tightens this to "check `ls $(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/nexus-claims` before every test or live run".
- A slice claim and a `FILE_<path>` hot-file claim are needed before edits. `GATEWAY` is needed for any inference run.
- Live claims right now: `PR_434`, `V114_INTEGRATION_LANE` and `WP_PROVIDER_WAIT_RESUME`, plus `FILE_cli_src_agent.ts.handoff-20261109T155819Z`. There is no `SUITE` claim at the moment. Other entries are `released-*`.
